record.program_name: Truckee Town-owned land public-private partnerships (Edmunds Lofts) and Railyard Master Plan affordable housing obligations
record.administering_agency: Town of Truckee Planning Division and Town Manager
record.typical_award_size: Edmunds Lofts: Town-owned 0.5-acre site (APN 018-580-052, dedicated by High Altitude Fitness) to be conveyed to Paradigm8 / Sagemodern under a Development and Disposition Agreement for 12 deed-restricted workforce units; entitlements granted in 2025 and building permits under review (75% complete at December 31, 2025). Railyard: Council work plan item 6.3 will move inclusionary and workforce housing obligations from the Railyard Development Agreement into the Railyard Master Plan (late 2026 to early 2027); the Town made a significant financial contribution to the earlier 66-unit Truckee Artist Lofts in the Railyard. Draft 7th cycle Program H-2.H directs annual review of all Town-owned and partner-agency land (TTUSD, Caltrans, Tahoe Forest Hospital, Truckee Donner PUD) for housing.
record.per_unit_cap: Land contribution; no cash figure published.
record.affordability_requirement: Deed-restricted workforce units per the DDA; Railyard units per the Development Agreement.
record.next_deadline: No open RFIQ as of 2026-11-08. Council removed the pilot to find another site from the 2025-2027 work plan on September 9, 2025. Watch the Railyard Master Plan amendment (late 2026 to early 2027).
record.layering_notes: Land write-downs of public land are public subsidy for prevailing wage purposes and trigger Surplus Land Act review. Coldstream Commons (48 units at 60% AMI, nine HUD 811 units) is an existing affordable project in the Coldstream Specific Plan area; no new Coldstream affordable commitment was found this pass. Prohousing Designation status for Truckee was not confirmed.
record.cycle_notes: no open solicitation; RFIQ issued October 16, 2024

record.program_name: Grass Valley Affordable Housing Density Bonuses and Incentives (Development Code Chapter 17.32)
record.administering_agency: City of Grass Valley Community Development Department
record.typical_award_size: Incentive, not a subsidy. Local chapter tracks Government Code 65915: one incentive at 10% lower income, 5% very low or 10% moderate (common interest) units, two at 17% lower or 10% very low, and so on; parking reductions (17.32.050) and childcare bonuses (17.32.060); Council grants requested incentives unless it makes written findings. The 2024 Annual Progress Report says no density bonus has been requested and the City planned updates to the ordinance.
record.affordability_requirement: Per Government Code 65915; density bonus agreement under 17.32.100.
record.next_deadline: Not applicable; requested before or with the project application.
record.layering_notes: Grass Valley has no inclusionary ordinance, no city housing trust fund of its own and no city NOFA; its local money flows through the Western Nevada County Regional Housing Trust Fund and the regional PLHA plan administered by Nevada County HCS (see county records). Code text read from the zoneomics mirror; grassvalleyca.gov returns a JavaScript shell to scripts, so the City's meeting-host attachments were used for the APR.
